# NORMAL vs not-NORMAL (trained screen)


Among usable breasts, train a binary screen: **NORMAL** vs **not-NORMAL** (BENIGN or CANCER). Features are summaries of that breast’s usable scans — mean water-peak height, within-breast SD of that height, how many usable scans, and Water:Fat of the breast mean — not the raw curve (which barely helps once the water filter has already selected glandular tissue). Scores are **out-of-fold** from **GroupKFold by patient**, so a breast is never scored by a model that saw its contralateral side.

::: {#cell-fig-normal-model .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, roc_curve
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# one row per usable breast
_nn_items = []  # nova, side, label, features
for (nova, side, label), curves in breast_use.items():
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        mean_curve = np.nanmean(curves, axis=0)
        water_heights = [float(np.nanmean(c[(q >= WATER[0]) & (q <= WATER[1])])) for c in curves]
    wf = water_fat(mean_curve)
    _nn_items.append((nova, side, label, np.array([
        np.mean(water_heights),
        np.std(water_heights) if len(water_heights) > 1 else 0.0,
        len(curves),
        wf if np.isfinite(wf) else np.nan,
    ])))

_nn_X = np.vstack([feat for *_, feat in _nn_items])
_nn_wf_fill = np.nanmedian(_nn_X[:, 3])
_nn_X[np.isnan(_nn_X[:, 3]), 3] = _nn_wf_fill
_nn_y = np.array([0 if label == "NORMAL" else 1 for *_, label, _ in _nn_items])  # 1 = not-NORMAL
_nn_g = np.array([nova for nova, *_ in _nn_items])
_nn_labels = np.array([label for *_, label, _ in _nn_items])
_nn_feature_names = ("water height", "within-breast SD", "usable scans", "Water:Fat")

_nn_cv = GroupKFold(n_splits=min(5, len(np.unique(_nn_g))))
_nn_model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=3000, class_weight="balanced", C=0.1))
_nn_proba = np.full(len(_nn_y), np.nan)
for _tr, _te in _nn_cv.split(_nn_X, _nn_y, _nn_g):
    _nn_model.fit(_nn_X[_tr], _nn_y[_tr])
    _nn_proba[_te] = _nn_model.predict_proba(_nn_X[_te])[:, 1]
_nn_auc = roc_auc_score(_nn_y, _nn_proba)
_nn_fpr, _nn_tpr, _ = roc_curve(_nn_y, _nn_proba)
_nn_proba_by_label = {lab: _nn_proba[_nn_labels == lab] for lab in COHORTS}
_nn_medians = {lab: float(np.median(v)) if len(v) else np.nan for lab, v in _nn_proba_by_label.items()}
_nn_counts = {lab: int((_nn_labels == lab).sum()) for lab in COHORTS}

# coefficients on the full set (for reading direction only; scores above are CV)
_nn_model.fit(_nn_X, _nn_y)
_nn_coef = dict(zip(_nn_feature_names, _nn_model.named_steps["logisticregression"].coef_.ravel()))

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, (roc_ax, score_ax) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.8))
for ax in (roc_ax, score_ax):
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)

roc_ax.plot(_nn_fpr, _nn_tpr, color="#1f2d4a", lw=1.8, label=f"AUC = {_nn_auc:.2f}")
roc_ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color="grey", ls="--", lw=1)
roc_ax.set(xlabel="false positive rate", ylabel="true positive rate",
           title="NORMAL vs not-NORMAL (usable breasts)", xlim=(0, 1), ylim=(0, 1))
roc_ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="lower right", fontsize=6)
roc_ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

_rng_sc = np.random.default_rng(4)
box_with_points(score_ax, [(k, _nn_proba_by_label[lab], ne.STATUS_COLOURS[lab])
                           for k, lab in enumerate(COHORTS) if len(_nn_proba_by_label[lab])], _rng_sc)
score_ax.set_xticks(range(3))
score_ax.set_xticklabels([f"{lab}\n(n = {_nn_counts[lab]})" for lab in COHORTS], fontsize=6)
score_ax.set(ylabel="P(not-NORMAL), out-of-fold", title="CV score by true label", ylim=(0, 1))
score_ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

70 usable NORMAL and 179 usable not-NORMAL breasts
(136 BENIGN, 43 CANCER), from 164 patients.
Out-of-fold AUC for NORMAL vs not-NORMAL is **0\.61**. Median P(not-NORMAL):
0\.47 (NORMAL),
0\.50 (BENIGN),
0\.49 (CANCER).

This is a **screen against the normal pool**, not a BENIGN vs CANCER classifier — those two stay close (@fig-normal-model). The fitted directions (full-data coefficients, for reading only):
water height \+0\.23\, within\-breast SD \-0\.35\, usable scans \+0\.26\, Water:Fat \+0\.25.
Curve-shape models on the same split do no better once the water filter has already kept glandular scans.
